correctness.rationale: The exact two-bidder externality identity R=max(a,b)+max(c,d)-max(a+d,b+c) reduces all cases to independent signed preference gaps. The quadrant case distinction gives the distribution-free local derivatives and the precise decline event; symmetric unimodality makes the translated gap magnitude stochastically increase, proving mean monotonicity. A continuous bimodal counterexample is bounded by a rigorous Lipschitz comparison with the exactly evaluated Rademacher gaps. For Uniform cells, triangular density integration gives closed-form probability, expected loss, expected gain, and expected revenue, including correct joins at shocks 1 and 2. Delivered checker.py was run from the actual scientific package and passed 7,776 exact finite grid/shock checks, nine symbolic integration identities, 700,000 uniform simulations and 120,000 bimodal simulations. Continuous and infinite parameter claims are proven analytically, not inferred from finite tests.

value.rationale: Hartline gives a minimal deterministic revenue-drop example but not a risk characterization. This theorem quantifies exactly how prevalent negative revenue shocks are (a distribution-free 1/8 local incidence and full exact shock curve) and separates ex-post risk from ex-ante monotonicity using an interpretable symmetric-unimodality condition. The atomless bimodal construction establishes a real structural assumption boundary. Exact expected loss and expected change quantify economic materiality in the canonical smallest substitutable-goods market; these are natural comparative-static quantities, not arbitrary slice parameters.
